statements.t: Due to market tightness driven by limited equipment availability and minimal indications of budget exhaustion, we expect less seasonality next quarter than what we have historically experienced.
Further, although hydraulic fracturing economics are improving, we believe capital discipline will exacerbate tightening supply demand balances for equipment.
In Proppant Production , ProFrac expects fourth quarter 2026 results to improve relative to the third quarter, reflecting recovering throughput at the Company’s West Texas operations.
Excluding Flotek, the Company expects that capital expenditures will be in a range of $145 million to $165 million for 2026.
The Company anticipates that subsequent events and developments will cause its assessments to change.

risks.t: the failure to operationalize or utilize to the extent anticipated the Company’s fleets and sand mines in a timely manner or at all
the risk that the Company may need more capital than it currently projects or that capital expenditures could increase beyond current expectations
risks regarding the ability to access additional capital on acceptable terms or at all
the availability, timing, and terms of financing or other support from related parties or other sources
industry conditions, including fluctuations in supply, demand and prices for the Company’s products and services and for oil and natural gas
the effectiveness of the Company’s risk management strategies
